Source: the derivative DG(x) v = (v, Du(x) v) of the graph parametrization used in Steps 3, 5 and 6 of the parent proof (tau_x = DG(x)(R^n) = {(v, Du(x) v)}).

1. The pairing map Gamma : R^n x R^l -> R^(n+l), Gamma(v, w) := graphPoint v w = toLp (Fin.append (ofLp v) (ofLp w)), is R-linear. Indeed, by Fin.addCases every index of Fin (n+l) is either Fin.castAdd l j (j < n) or Fin.natAdd n k (k < l), and by Fin.append_left / Fin.append_right the corresponding coordinates of graphPoint v w are v_j and w_k respectively; these coordinate functions are additive and homogeneous in (v, w), so graphPoint (v + v') (w + w') = graphPoint v w + graphPoint v' w' and graphPoint (c v) (c w) = c graphPoint v w (compare coordinates). Since R^n x R^l is finite-dimensional, Gamma is a continuous linear map (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap), and hence HasFDerivAt Gamma Gamma p at every point p (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt).
2. Since u is differentiable at x, HasFDerivAt u (Du(x)) x, and the map z -> (z, u(z)) has derivative v -> (v, Du(x) v) at x (HasFDerivAt.prodMk of hasFDerivAt_id and the derivative of u).
3. G = Gamma o (z -> (z, u z)). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp), G has derivative Gamma o (v -> (v, Du(x) v)) at x. In particular G is differentiable at x, and by uniqueness of the derivative (HasFDerivAt.fderiv) fderiv G x = Gamma o (id, Du(x)), so for every v in R^n, fderiv G x v = Gamma(v, Du(x) v) = graphPoint v (Du(x) v). This proves both conjuncts.

subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U an open subset of R^(n+l), h : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l), q a natural number, alpha real, xi in R^(n+l) and Q a linear isometry equivalence of R^(n+l). If h is locally C^{q,alpha} in U (IsLocallyHolderCkα q alpha h U: h is C^q on U and for every compact K contained in U there is C with |D^q h(a) - D^q h(b)| <= C |a - b|^alpha for a, b in K), then O is open and F is locally C^{q,alpha} in O.

Source: Step 1 of the parent proof (invariance of the local Hoelder class under the affine isometry A(z) = xi + Q^{-1} z). All lemmas used are reachable from the frozen imports of GMT.Ch05.Submission.

Notation: T(y) := Q(y - xi) and A(z) := xi + Q^{-1} z. D^j denotes iteratedFDeriv R j (the global iterated Frechet derivative, as in IsLocallyHolderCkα).
1. T and A are mutually inverse: A(T y) = xi + Q^{-1} Q (y - xi) = y and T(A z) = Q(Q^{-1} z) = z. Both are isometries: |T y - T y'| = |Q(y - y')| = |y - y'| and |A z - A z'| = |Q^{-1}(z - z')| = |z - z'|. Both are continuous (a constant plus a continuous linear map, composed with a translation).
2. O is open. Since T and A are inverse bijections, O = T(U) = A^{-1}(U) (Set.image_eq_preimage_of_inverse). A is continuous and U is open, so A^{-1}(U) is open (IsOpen.preimage).
3. F is C^q on O. By hypothesis h is C^q on U. A is C^infinity (constant plus continuous linear map) and maps O into U (A(T y) = y in U for y in U), so h o A is C^q on O (ContDiffOn.comp). Q is a continuous linear map, hence C^infinity, so F = Q o (h o A) is C^q on O (ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn).
4. Formula for D^q F at an arbitrary point z (no smoothness is needed for these identities). Write h o A = (h o tau) o Q^{-1} with tau(w) := xi + w. The compact set K := G(tsupport phi). tsupport phi is compact (HasCompactSupport) and contained in Bo^n_r(0), where G is continuous (u is continuous there and graphPoint is continuous); hence K is compact (IsCompact.image_of_continuousOn), and K is contained in Bo_s(0) by the hypothesis |G(x)| < s on Bo^n_r(0). K is closed, so by exists_lt_subset_ball there is s1 < s with K contained in Bo_{s1}(0). Put s' := max(s1, s/2) and s'' := (s' + s)/2; then 0 < s' < s'' < s and K is contained in Bo_{s'}(0).
2. Cutoff. Let psi be the smooth bump function (ContDiffBump) centered at 0 with inner radius s' and outer radius s'': psi is C^infinity (ContDiffBump.contDiff), psi = 1 on the closed ball B_{s'}(0) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall), and the support of psi is the open ball Bo_{s''}(0) (ContDiffBump.support_eq).
3. Definition. Xt(z) := psi(z) * iota(phi(pi z)) and X(y) := Q^{-1}(Xt(T y)).

Regularity and support. pi, iota, Q^{-1} and T (Q composed with a translation) are C^infinity, phi is C^1 and psi is C^infinity, so X is C^1 (ContDiff.smul, ContDiff.comp; psi is C^1 since C^infinity implies C^1). If X(y) != 0 then psi(T y) != 0, so |T y| = |y - xi| < s''. Hence the support of X is contained in Bo_{s''}(xi), its closure tsupport X is contained in the closed ball B_{s''}(xi), which is contained in Bo_s(xi) because s'' < s, and X has compact support because B_{s''}(xi) is compact (proper space; a closed subset of a compact set is compact).

If x is in tsupport phi, then G x is in K, contained in B_{s'}(0), so psi(G x) = 1 and X(y0) = Q^{-1}(iota(phi x)). If x is not in tsupport phi, then phi(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so X(y0) = Q^{-1}(psi(G x) iota 0) = 0 = Q^{-1}(iota(phi x)). In both cases X(y0) = Q^{-1}(graphPoint 0 (phi x)).
